Please review the following manuscript. I feel disappointed with this paper. My overall impression is poor, and I'd be concerned to see it accepted.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b09/review-experiment-zxxdns1j/call-78766881f8b44b6b91585e0709e8f4c7/manuscript.pdf

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r = PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('Pages:', len(r.pages))
print('Metadata:', r.metadata)
text = '\\n\\n'.join(f'--- PAGE {i+1} ---\\n'+p.extract_text() for i,p in enumerate(r.pages))
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text(text)
print(text[:30000])
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re
s=Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').read_text()
s=re.sub(r'/uni[0-9a-fA-F]{8}', '', s)
s=re.sub(r'\\n{3,}', '\\n\\n', s)
Path('tmp/pdfs/clean.txt').write_text(s)
print(s[s.index('--- PAGE 9 ---'):])
PY"

strengths: The paper addresses an important question: why learning return distributions can improve reinforcement learning even when decisions use expected returns. A regularization interpretation could provide useful insight.

The experiments reveal interesting task-dependent interactions between distributional critics and policy entropy, particularly on Swimmer and BipedalWalkerHardcore. The factorial comparisons across eight continuous-control environments are useful empirical observations.

The manuscript provides pseudocode, hyperparameters, and results over multiple seeds. It also explicitly acknowledges that the theoretical analysis concerns KL-based methods and that the quantile extension is heuristic.
weaknesses: The foundational decomposition requires stronger conditions than the paper acknowledges. Equation (4) requires an atom of mass 1−ε at the exact return mean; general continuous distributions lack this atom, so the proposed subtraction cannot produce a probability measure. Proposition 1 supplies a CDF approximation without controlling the resulting KL objective. Furthermore, KL from this mixed atomic target to an absolutely continuous critic is infinite, undermining the density-based derivation of Proposition 3. A consistent measure-theoretic or discrete formulation is needed.

The main explanatory connection is unsupported. Minimizing cross-entropy when fitting a critic does not establish that the policy maximizes the cross-entropy reward bonus introduced in Equations (8)–(10). With exact return distributions, the stated mean-greedy policy is indifferent between equal-mean actions with different return entropies; the proposed augmented objective can prefer one. Thus the augmented objective describes a modified algorithm, and its equivalence to ordinary distributional RL is not demonstrated. Cross-entropy also includes prediction mismatch, so interpreting it directly as environmental dispersion or reducible uncertainty is unjustified.

The convergence and algorithm derivations contain substantive gaps. Appendix D treats the entropy-augmented reward as unchanged during policy improvement, although its return distributions and critic depend on the policy. Boundedness alone does not justify that step. In Equation (12), expanding the squared residual produces the cross term 2E[δ√(λH)], where δ is the ordinary Bellman residual. The assumption E[δ]=0 does not eliminate this term because H can depend on δ through the state, action, and critic. Consequently, neither the claimed policy-iteration guarantee nor the derivation of the implemented interpolation loss is established.

The experiments support performance observations more strongly than the proposed mechanism. Section 4.1 redefines ε and modifies target probabilities without demonstrating that this isolates the regularizer in Equation (6). The IQN comparisons change the critic formulation without establishing a corresponding entropy decomposition. Returns alone do not demonstrate risk-sensitive exploration, reduced intrinsic uncertainty, or interference between exploration gradients. Learning curves also cannot validate the disputed convergence argument.

Reproducibility remains incomplete despite the appendix. The exact probability-mass redistribution rule, categorical support limits, Atari preprocessing and training protocol, and interpretation of shaded uncertainty bands are insufficiently specified. No implementation is linked. The target-modification details are especially consequential for reproducing the central ablation.

The relationship to directly relevant prior explanations is insufficiently developed. The paper omits substantive comparison with Lyle et al., A Comparative Analysis of Expected and Distributional Reinforcement Learning (2019), and Imani and White, Improving Regression Performance with Distributional Losses (2018). Since the central loss decomposition largely follows from linearity of cross-entropy, the manuscript needs to establish what additional explanatory or predictive insight it contributes beyond existing distributional-loss and representation-learning accounts.
